### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **37** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/template.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via FlowValueSlotSchema (symbol, a top-level const object), daysAgo (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro), isoDate (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro; a string literal in dateMacroRemedy), isoDatetime (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro; a string literal in dateMacroRemedy))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro), isoDate (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro; a string literal in dateMacroRemedy), isoDatetime (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro; a string literal in dateMacroRemedy))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/schema.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in celDateMacro))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/template.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2bb1f3b241c770f1f495d3cce52b04b169ef8d83` — the merge of head `3c97f71067e95a79b91f3008353b1b5660e98586` into base `f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2bb1f3b241c770f1f495d3cce52b04b169ef8d83 && git checkout 2bb1f3b241c770f1f495d3cce52b04b169ef8d83
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19 3c97f71067e95a79b91f3008353b1b5660e98586 && git checkout -B drift-repro f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19 && git merge --no-ff 3c97f71067e95a79b91f3008353b1b5660e98586

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3c97f71067e95a79b91f3008353b1b5660e98586`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #19939 (body and all 27 comments, the pass-3 claim `6093076978`, the carries `6067854904` / `6092547738` / `6092730938`, seat 3's pointer `6094071127`, the pass-2 landing `6093042228`, the dev report `6095185806`), ruling D on #11182 (`5805777944`), PR #22635 (body, 24 files, the net diff from merge base `e22315238f`: +1351 / −271, patch-id `51dd1d8bb044`), the check-runs on the head, and `main` as read. Nothing was built, run or re-run; every code reading below is of the head or of `origin/main` through `git show` / `git grep`.

### ① Derived judgments

**The refusal — accept set, `@objectstack/spec`. RIGHT.** `valueSlotTemplateRefusals` drops `KEPT_KINDS`; the only early return left on a string is `tokens.length === 0`, so a value slot keeps NO single-brace token. The doors are wired at the head and read, not run: the Zod contracts (`celValueSlotSchema` → `valueSlotTemplateRefusals`, `builtin-node-config.zod.ts:359`; the `AssignmentConfigSchema` catchall with `envelopeIsLiteral`, `:1106`), `objectstack validate` (`validate-expressions.ts:2376`), `registerFlow` (`engine.ts:4497` → `validateFlowExpressions` → `:10808`), the executors (CRUD through `parseNodeConfig` / `FlowValueSlotSchema`; assignment at `logic-nodes.ts:164`). Pinned at each: every value-slot contract refuses `{TODAY() + 7}` and accepts its envelope; `AssignmentConfigSchema.safeParse({ assignments: { due: '{TODAY() + 7}' } })` is false; registration pins in `logic-nodes.test.ts` and `crud-fields-value-envelope.test.ts` name the node, the path and the form; the validate pin in `validate-expressions.fields-value-slot.test.ts` (`expression-invalid`, error, located) carries three macro rows and the mixed-token row. Alone, with `± N`, with a variable or junk offset, beside text, beside another token — all refused (judge pins at eleven spellings plus the edges and the leak). Ablation A1 (judge keeps the kind again → 23 red) is reported, not re-run.

**The CEL string forms. RIGHT**, checked against `main`'s `builtin/template.ts` `resolveToken` (UTC-only since #14852: `setUTCDate(getUTCDate() + sign * offset)`, then `toISOString()` for `NOW()` and `.slice(0, 10)` for `TODAY()`) and against `main`'s `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts`, which this PR does not touch: `isoDate` is `toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, `isoDatetime` is `toISOString()`, `addDays(d, n)` is `setUTCDate(getUTCDate() + Math.trunc(Number(n)))`, `daysFromNow(int)` / `daysAgo(int)` are the calendar day ± n, `today()` is `calendarDayUtc(now(), tz)` with `tz` defaulting to `'UTC'`. `celDateMacro` mirrors `resolveToken` byte for byte: the same `DATE_MACRO` regex, `Number(offset)` first, else a variable path, else nothing; a zero offset is skipped as `if (offset)` skips it; a signed literal after the sign composes as the template composes it (`{TODAY() + -3}` → `daysAgo(3)`). So `{TODAY()}` → `isoDate(today())`; `{TODAY() ± N}` → `isoDate(daysFromNow(N))` / `isoDate(daysAgo(N))` (the date part of calendar day ± N, which is what the template's `.slice(0, 10)` wrote); `{NOW()}` → `isoDatetime(now())`; `{NOW() ± N}` → `isoDatetime(addDays(now(), ±N))`, right because `daysFromNow` starts from UTC midnight and the template kept the time of day (ablation A2 reports the pin catching exactly the midnight form); `{TODAY() + days}` → `isoDate(addDays(today(), days))`. The three edges are named right: a fraction (the template truncated the SUM inside `setUTCDate`, `addDays` truncates the OFFSET; `daysFromNow(int)` refuses a double at build); a variable offset (the template did `variables.has(name)` on the whole text, no dotted walk, then `Number(v) || 0`; CEL reads the path, faults on an absent variable, and a non-number makes an invalid Date that `isoTimestampText` throws on); neither (`{TODAY() + 3d}` → 0 days, remedy `isoDate(today())` and says so). The text-with-holes form puts the macro's source in the concatenation (`'Due ' + isoDate(daysFromNow(7)) + ' for ' + name`), a string, so `+` is well typed.

**The parity pin. RIGHT, and it proves what the claim asks.** `crud-fields-value-envelope.test.ts` runs `interpolateString` and the envelope the judge PRINTS (`remedyOf` reads the source off the refusal, then asserts it equals the table's spelling — the table only names which spelling) through the engine and a real ObjectQL store, with `Date` frozen at five instants (a spring-forward and a fall-back day, the last millisecond of a month, a year end, a leap day), over thirteen spellings: the six whole-number forms, three variable offsets, the fraction, the junk offset, text with holes and the leak. The edges are pinned as named: `-1.5` lands a day apart on the 8th and agrees on the 1st; `daysAgo(1.5)` refused at registration; an absent or non-numeric `days` fails the run with the source and writes nothing. One reading for the seat, not a defect: parity is proven on the UTC reference calendar. `today()` is the reference-timezone day (ADR-0053 D1) and the flow engine passes no timezone — `celScope` returns `{ extra, record }` and `timezone` appears nowhere in `engine.ts` or `builtin/` — so `isoDate(today())` is the UTC day the template wrote. The remedy's "on the UTC calendar" is true of the engine as wired; if a flow run ever carries a reference timezone, that sentence and the near-midnight day would need re-reading.

**The kept-spelling leak (`6092730938`). RIGHT.** `'Due {TODAY()} by {$User.Id}'` is refused with one concatenation and one sentence per token (the run user's guard included); pinned in the judge, at the validate door and in the parity pin.

**Literal-data positions, option A judge-side (`6092547738` item 1). RIGHT, and inside the carry.** The carry says the envelope remedy "has held since pass 1 for every `{…}` token there" and asks for one of two routes "with a pin through the engine". The dev took the judge-side route, said why (an envelope there is data today, pinned by `the legacy shapes are untouched` and the CRUD nested-envelope pin; evaluating it would change what an existing flow writes and needs a ledger declaration), and pinned it through the engine: `assignment-value-envelope.test.ts` (both legacy shapes → the canonical map writes `'Hello Ada'`; the nested map literal writes the template's object; the mixed map evaluates only with `dyn(…)`; controls store the envelope object) and `crud-fields-value-envelope.test.ts` (the nested CRUD string). Naming it for every token is not a widening: `literalPositionLead` is positional (a legacy shape, or a non-empty path inside the slot value), the per-token remedy is unchanged, and the top-level declared slot keeps the envelope remedy (control pinned). The text is right: `literalAlong` builds the map/list literal along the path with CEL string keys and list indices (`[x]`, `{'meta': {'note': 'for ' + name}}`); the `dyn(…)` sentence matches the pinned registration refusal of the un-wrapped mixed map; the lint hints inherit it by asking the judge at the position (`valueSlotSpellingAt`).

**The `has()` guard (`6094071127`). RIGHT.** `guardOf` now prints `has(vars.a) && has(vars.a.b) && … ? vars.a.b : null`. The semantics claim holds: `has(e.f)` evaluates `e` and tests `f`, so `has(source.id)` evaluates the unbound `source`; `vars` is a plain map `celScope` builds from the bound variables alone (it iterates `variables`, then binds `vars` and `current_user` over the spread), so `has(vars.source)` is a key test that cannot fault, and `&&` stops at the first `false`. Pinned through the engine with an unsupplied `isInput` variable and no default (`value-slot-template-grammar.test.ts`: `execute(…, { params: {} })` → `{ who: null }`; control `has(source.id) ? …` → `Unknown variable: source`), and at the unit level for unbound, `null`, absent-key and bound over four shapes. The lint hint carries the judge's words (pinned not to contain `has(source.id)`), the D3 entry's acceptance criteria carry the chain, and the old `celHeadReadsThroughVars` branch in `guardOf` is gone, rightly: every head is selected off `vars` now, and `vars` holds every bound variable.

**The text-slot judge. RIGHT, forced.** Its date-macro remedy named `assignments: { v: '{TODAY() + 7}' }`, a spelling this change refuses; it now names the envelope of the string form with the edge sentence, and `18.flow-text-slot-single-brace-refused.ts`'s replacement says the same.

**`@objectstack/lint`. RIGHT, patch-level.** `flow-double-brace-interpolation` in a value slot now names the envelope for the holes the author meant (`DOUBLE_BRACE_HOLES` → single-brace tokens → the judge at the position) where it named `{record.title}`, which the slot refuses; `flow-bare-dollar-reference` asks the judge at the position (`valueSlotRefusalAt` returns the label and the path), so a nested or legacy-shape string gets the spelling that evaluates there. No rule added, no severity moved; the double-brace finding's message text changes in value slots only. The two #1315 guards are re-titled with their assertions unchanged.

**Descriptions, docs, README. RIGHT.** The two `.describe()` strings and the regenerated `builtin-node-config.mdx`, `flows.mdx` (FROM → TO rows, the literal-data paragraph, the dialect table, the failure modes, the guard row), the published `service-automation` README and the three docblocks no longer say the macros are kept or that CEL has no string form.

**Public surface. RIGHT — nothing new reaches an entry.** The diff adds exactly two `export` lines, `celDateMacro` and `CelDateMacro`, both in `flow-template-token.ts`; `automation/index.ts` re-exports `flow-value-slot-template` and `flow-text-slot-template` and not the token module; spec's `exports` map has no wildcard subpath; no `api-surface/**` or `export-origins/**` file is among the 24, and `api-surface/automation.json` at the head still lists the same functions. No export is removed.

**Census. Consistent.** No `examples/**` file is in the diff, and at the head `git grep` finds no single-brace date macro string in `examples/**` or `packages/**/src/**` outside tests and docs except the comment at `validate-field-consumers.ts:335`, which the dev lists in the Acceptance notes.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/spec` major, `@objectstack/service-automation` major — RIGHT for the v18 line.** An accept-set narrowing on a published authoring surface (`FlowValueSlotSchema` / `AssignmentValueSchema` and the catchall). `.changeset/pre.json` on `main` reads `mode: pre`, `tag: next`, so the release is `18.0.0-next.*`; triage `6038868940` grades a breaking change landing after #22080 as `major`; pass 1 (`6058684331`) and pass 2 (`6092730938`) graded the same two packages major under at-tier PASS records. The `fixed` group in `.changeset/config.json` holds spec, lint and service-automation together, so the group takes the highest bump in any case. The BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO table and the ADR-0087 marker are present.
- **`@objectstack/lint` patch — RIGHT.** Lint's own surface (rules, exports, severities) is unchanged; its diff is hint and message text, and the `expression-invalid` narrowing arrives through spec's judge. This is pass 2's level for lint (pass 1 graded lint major), so the PR body's "pass 1 and pass 2's levels" is pass 2's for this package — a wording slip, not a grading error.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — RIGHT, and the right spelling.** Confirmed as above: nothing new reaches a package entry, no snapshot moved, `check:api-surface` / `check:export-origins` run in `Lint & Repo Gates`, which is green on this head. The precedent `72af58c621` took `yes (narrowing)` because its new exports `checkPageRequiresKind` and `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS` entered `api-surface/ui.json`; this diff enters nothing there, so the pair is `no` with its direction arm, the spelling pass 2 took for the same reason and the one the dispatch prescribes. The claim line reads `no`, the same value without the arm; the PR body and the changeset carry the arm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Surface crossings — accepted, each forced.** `crud-nodes.ts` / `logic-nodes.ts` (docblocks that said the macros reach `interpolate()`); `flow-text-slot-template.ts`, its test and `18.flow-text-slot-single-brace-refused.ts` (a remedy that named a refused spelling); `builtin-node-config.test.ts`, `logic-nodes.test.ts`, `value-slot-template-grammar.test.ts`, `assignment-value-envelope.test.ts` (pinned the kept spelling; the last two now host the engine pins the carries require). No governed path among the 24 files.
- **ADR-0087 — legal, and the entries cover the change.** The ADR's closed vocabulary admits `not-required (already-registered id, …)` when every named id pre-dates the merge base; `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` verifies resolve-at-HEAD and exist-at-base, and both ids do (pass 1 registered `flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused`, #22110 registered `flow-text-slot-single-brace-refused`); the `Require an ADR-0087 disposition` step is green on this head. The ADR says the gate never verifies COVERAGE, so read for it: the amended entry's surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria name the macros, their four forms, the three edges, the literal-data positions and the chain guard; D3's one-entry-per-retirement-family holds (no second entry for the family); the entries sit on the unreleased `18.0.0-next` line, so no shipped chain step is rewritten. `registry.ts` carries the same text in the generated step and the hand-kept `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment. Precedent: pass 2 amended the same entry with the same marker under an at-tier PASS. No D2 conversion — right, the fraction and the silent-zero cases are not lossless.
- **`main` moved — checked with the compare.** At this read `main` is `1b99388505`, one commit past the `f368b7e980` the dev reported (#22632, `fix(service-automation): the run row's highlight set …`, touching `engine.ts`, `index.ts`, `sys-automation-run.object.ts` and a test). `compare 3c97f71067...main`: 7 commits ahead, 75 paths, 0 of them among the PR's 24; `registry.ts` is not among them; the PR reads `mergeable: true`. The dev's "share no path" holds for all seven, so no third merge was owed for this review; CI runs on the merge ref.
- **Check-runs on the head:** read 2026-10-10T07:57Z: 34 check-runs, 33 completed (31 success, 2 skipped, 0 failure), 1 still in progress (Test Core (4/6)). The in-progress ones are not judged green by this record; the seat reads them settled before enqueue. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts.
- **Out-of-scope (1): `record` with no `record` variable — escalated, needs its own card (does not block this PR).** Read at the head: `celScope` returns `{ extra: { ...vars, vars, current_user }, record: vars }`, so the formula engine's `record` binding IS the variables map whenever the flow binds no `record` variable, and `record.assignee` silently reads a variable named `assignee` instead of faulting. The dev measured it through `evaluateValueEnvelope` only, but the executors call that primitive with `celScope`, and `registerFlow` + `execute` are public doors — one call away, un-gated. It is the silent-tolerance class, with a named producer (`celScope`, `record: vars`), and the nuance the card must carry: `record: vars` is also how bare variable names resolve in flow CEL, so the fix is a scope decision (mount bare names through `extra` only; bind `record` only when a `record` variable exists), not a one-liner. Not caused by this PR; the judge's chain guard reads `vars.record` and does not trip it.
- **Out-of-scope (2)–(5) — carried right.** #22586 (open, `pm:blocked`) is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION card; the seat should append the three rows this PR supersedes (pass 1's and pass 2's `19939-*` changesets, `22110-flow-text-slot-double-brace.md`) to its list. #22585 (open, skills lane) carries `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`. The two stale comments (`validate-field-consumers.ts:335`, `flow-node-expression-paths.test.ts:130`) stay Acceptance notes — no regeneration is owed. HotCRM's 15 date-macro sites go to seat post #6017's cross-repo ledger.
- **PR #22609 (seat 3, open):** adds 5 fixture lines to `lint-flow-patterns.test.ts`, measured disjoint from this PR's hunks (`6094071127`); the later lander merges `main`.
- **Dev deviations answered:** a fifth ablation (A5, the guard) beyond the order's four — welcome; the Clause-② arm (claim `no`, PR `no (narrowing)`) — same value, above; the attribution trailer form — AGENTS.md's; the stray `/abl-A2.pid` the dev reports at its container's filesystem root is outside the repository and the diff — nothing in this record acts on it.
- **Six rider positions:** untouched, as the claim forbids; the carry line on #19939 (`6092730938`) stands.

Reviewed-by: `session_01VZqqwTj2wsihZEbfT6yyYN`

**VERDICT: PASS**
